incident-bot: PAGE: INC-2028 - Embeddings ingestion error rate > 5% across us-east ingest cluster. Auto-escalation to oncall.
Aisha.khan: I'm taking primary for the handoff. Current summary: embeddings ingestion (ingest-worker pool) is returning 500s for ~6% of requests since ~17:42 UTC. Customer-visible: a subset of indexing jobs failing with transient errors; embeddings requests are retried by upstream service but latency spikes. Impact: partial index delays for a few mid-market customers, no data loss confirmed yet.

Tom.garcia: I pushed a temporary routing rule 10m ago to send new traffic to us-west fallback; that reduced error rate from 12% -> 6% but not gone. I also scaled ingest-worker replicas +30% (applied to dedicated pool).

Priya.singh: Noticed the stacktrace in logs shows KV store timeouts hitting the embedding workers during cold-start bursts. Logs: `GET /embed -> downstream kv: timeout 50ms` repeating.

Aisha.khan: Mitigations in progress: 1) Tom -> revert recent image change that introduced a sync blocking call, 2) Jon -> increase connection pool to KV and enable extra retries in config, 3) Priya -> enable request-level circuit breaker for problematic request patterns.

jon.lee: I'm on KV changes now. Patching connection pool config to pool_size=120 (was 40) and bumping client timeout from 50ms -> 200ms in staging then prod. Will watch for increased QPS error reduction.

Tom.garcia: Reverted image deploy (rolled back ingest-worker:v1.5.2 -> v1.5.1) at 17:51 UTC. Rolling back reduced 500s ratio by ~40% in the canary. Monitoring shows fewer timeouts.

monitoring-bot: metric alert resolved: ingest.500_errors (canary) dropped below threshold. Global alert still firing in us-east main cluster.

Aisha.khan: Runbook references: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Embeddings+Ingest+Runbook. Key playbooks used: "kv-timeout-debug", "ingest-rollback-and-fallback". Follow checklist in runbook step 2 before promoting any new image.

Priya.singh: Short-term customer mitigations: enabling HTTP 429 -> queued requeue path for failing jobs and routing heavy customers to dedicated fallback ingress. This will add a ~500ms retry but prevents immediate failures.

Tom.garcia: Command I ran to rollback:
```
kubectl -n inference set image deploy/ingest-worker ingest-worker=ingest-worker:v1.5.1 --record
kubectl rollout status deploy/ingest-worker -n inference
```
Watch logs: `kubectl logs -f deploy/ingest-worker -n inference | grep kv:timeout`

Priya.singh: I applied temporary circuit-breaker config in prod with:
```
POST /config/service/ingest/circuit-breaker
{ "error_threshold_percentage": 25, "request_volume_threshold": 50, "sleep_window_ms": 20000 }
```
This should trip on bad patterns and route to fallback queue.

Aisha.khan: Current status summary for handoff: - Primary: aisha.khan (active) - Secondary: tom.garcia (available, patching done) - Active incident: INC-2028 (embeddings ingest errors) - Customer impact: degraded indexing for selected customers, retries in place, no confirmed data loss - Mitigations: rollback completed, KV pool tuned, circuit breaker enabled, fallback routing enabled - Next alert threshold: ingest.5xx_rate > 2% for 10m -> trigger paging escalation.

Priya.singh: Observability notes: check traces filtered by `service:ingest-worker` and tag `kv.timeout`. Dashboard: Observability -> Ingest -> Errors (shortcut). Also look at per-customer error_breakdown panel to identify affected tenants.

jon.lee: I'm watching KV metrics and will follow if latency > 150ms persists. If that's the case, we'll implement a read-only cache warmup for hot keys and set TTL to 5m.

Aisha.khan: Handoff instructions for next shift (please read): 1) Continue to monitor `ingest.500_errors` and `ingest.latency.p95` in us-east. 2) If 5xx > 2% for 10m, run the rollback (commands above) + increase worker replicas by another 25%. 3) If KV latency persists, enable cache-warmup play (runbook step 6). 4) Update incident doc (INC-2028) with any customer notices and times of mitigation changes. 5) If customer-facing SLA risk arises (error rate > 5% for 30m), escalate to oncall-lead + CSM.

Tom.garcia: One more note: we saw a pattern where bursty bulk-index jobs correlate with the spike. Consider applying short-term rate-limiter per-tenant (see runbook snippet) to flatten bursts.

Aisha.khan: Coverage gaps: no infra patch scheduled until 02:00 UTC; if issue persists overnight, please coordinate with infra on-call to approve emergency kernel/network tweak. Secondary (tom) will cover immediate changes but we need infra if kernel param tuning required.

Priya.singh: Leaving my contact: priya.singh (pager) if you need DB/KV credentials rotated for testing.

incident-bot: NOTE: Create incident doc: https://incidents.redwood.ai/INC-2028 (link created). Add timeline entries for rollback at 17:51 UTC.

Aisha.khan: I'm signing off at 18:00 UTC. Tom will be primary for the next 30 minutes then hand to Priya for overnight. Final status before handoff: ingest 5xx = 1.8% (steady), p95 latency = 420ms.

Tom.garcia: I'll take over now. If anything spikes I'll page @oncall-lead. Leaving a quick checklist pinned: rollback commands, circuit-breaker toggle, KV pool knobs, fallback-route toggle.

Priya.singh: Acknowledged. I will monitor logs for the next hour and prepare notes for overnight shift. Good luck and feel free to @mention me if the fallback queue grows > 1000 items.

Aisha.khan: Thanks team. Closing this thread for handoff notes. Remember to update INC-2028 doc with steps taken and any customer communications. :thumbsup:
